findings.title: Recorded inert statements leak into later, unrelated loads.
findings.body:
`inert_statement/2` facts are cleared only by `report_inert_statements`, which runs only after an outermost `load_metta_file` succeeds. Two cases leave facts behind:
- The load throws partway through, so the code after `setup_call_cleanup` never runs.
- Code is translated outside a file load: a runtime `eval`, a REPL or Python `process_metta_string`, or a function added with `add-atom`.

Those facts stay and are reported on the next unrelated file load. Under `--strict`, that load then fails with `inert_statements` for code it does not contain. Without `--strict`, warnings are attributed to the wrong load.

Fix: clear `inert_statement/2` at the start of each outermost load, run the report in the cleanup of the outermost load, and judge statements recorded outside any load when they are recorded (or drop them).

findings.title: The eta closure ignores head patterns and adds an extra result next to ordinary clauses of the same arity.
findings.body:
`assert_eta_closure` adds the fact `F(V1..VN, partial(F,[V1..VN]))` to the same predicate (F/(N+1)) that holds every ordinary clause of F at source arity N. That fact matches any arguments.

Example: `(= (f 0) (g 1))` (binary `g`) together with `(= (f $x) $x)`. Before this change, `(f 5)` returned `5`. Now it returns both `5` and `(partial f (5))`, and applying that closure fails because only the `(f 0)` clause exists at the higher arity. Any `(f k)` with no matching partial-bodied clause also gains a dead closure result. Under a det declaration, the extra clause can also cause overlapping-clause errors.

Fix: make the closure use the head patterns of the clauses that actually compile above N+1. For example, emit one closure per such clause with that clause's head arguments, or guard the closure with a check that a higher-arity clause matches. Otherwise, refuse to mix partial-bodied and ordinary clauses at the same source arity.
